neighbours.label: relating new ideas to known ones (analogies, metaphors, connecting to prior knowledge)
fire: Good teachers explain electricity through analogies with water in pipes.
The lecturer used metaphors to help us grasp how memory works.
Try linking each new word to something the child already knows.
She explained the cell by comparing it to a busy factory.
Learners remember more when new facts are tied to familiar experiences.
The coach related the drill to a game the players knew well.
Using everyday analogies made the physics lesson much clearer.
Students build understanding by connecting new material to prior knowledge.
quiet: Good teachers explain electricity through experiments with batteries and bulbs.
The lecturer used slides to help us grasp how memory works.
Try repeating each new word several times with the child.
She explained the cell by drawing a large diagram on the board.
Learners remember more when new facts are reviewed every week.
The coach timed the drill so the players stayed focused.
Using colourful handouts made the physics lesson much clearer.
Students build understanding by practising new material every day.

notes: card: analog/metaph/relate/connect to former knowledge; logit effect promotes familiar/analogy/relate.
